'''Software-defined radio (SDR)''' implements radio functions such as modulation, filtering, synchronization, and demodulation in software while retaining a configurable RF front end. This page is the entry point for SDR hardware, software, and projects at IHF.

== Overview ==

An SDR system normally consists of:

{| class="wikitable"
! Part
! Purpose
|-
| RF front end
| Converts between the antenna frequency and analog baseband or an intermediate frequency.
|-
| ADC and DAC
| Convert between analog signals and digital samples.
|-
| FPGA
| Performs time-critical processing such as interpolation, decimation, filtering, and sample transport.
|-
| Host interface
| Transfers samples and control data between the SDR and the host computer, for example through 10 Gigabit Ethernet.
|-
| Driver and signal-processing software
| Configures the radio and implements the application. IHF currently uses UHD and GNU Radio for the USRP platform described below.
|}

<pre>
Receive:  Antenna/RF input -> RF front end -> ADC -> FPGA -> host interface -> application
Transmit: Application -> host interface -> FPGA -> DAC -> RF front end -> antenna/RF output
</pre>

The usable bandwidth and sample rate are limited by the complete chain: RF front end, converters, FPGA configuration, host interface, and host processing capacity.

== Software ==

The current USRP workflow uses:

* '''UHD''' to discover, configure, and stream samples to and from the USRP;
* '''GNU Radio''' to build and run signal-processing flowgraphs;
* '''Python''' for custom GNU Radio blocks, automation, and result visualization; and
* '''Git''' for version-controlled project development. See [[GIT - Versionskontrolle]].

Keep reusable installation and troubleshooting guidance on the hardware page. Keep project algorithms, parameters, results, and source-code instructions on the corresponding project page or in its repository.

== General RF practice ==

* Check the frequency, power, impedance, and connector ratings of every component before connecting it.
* Use suitable attenuation and 50-ohm terminations for conducted measurements.
* Keep RF outputs disabled while changing cables or instruments.
* Never exceed the maximum input level of an SDR or measurement instrument.
* Do not infer RF channel or connector mappings from Ethernet ports. Record the mapping reported by the driver.
* Record hardware identifiers, software versions, clock and sample rates, center frequency, gain, bandwidth, and runtime warnings with every measurement.
